SidComment: Exactly the four operations the reminder path performs, and no more.
Query  - list_by_provider_and_day reads PK=PROV#<id>, SK begins_with
APPT#<day>#, which is a main-table query.
GetItem- reading a patient record and the clinic knowledge base.
Scan   - non-obvious, and omitting it is how this fails at six in the
evening with AccessDenied: mark_reminded resolves an
appointment id through _find_by_entity_id, which is a filtered
scan, because the single-table key is composite and the id
alone does not carry it.
PutItem- also non-obvious. mark_reminded writes the whole item back
rather than patching a field, so this needs PutItem and NOT
UpdateItem.
Deliberately absent: DeleteItem and BatchWriteItem. A reminder run has
no business removing an appointment, and a role that cannot delete
cannot delete by accident.
sns:Publish with no Resource is how SNS sends to a bare phone number:
an SMS to a PhoneNumber has no topic ARN to scope to. Grants no topic
or subscription management - this sends one message per patient, it
does not administer a messaging platform.
A reminder run that fails silently is worse than one that never ran,
because the clinic then believes those patients were told. The log is
the only place a failed evening becomes visible.
One function, one action. The schedule's whole authority is 'start the
reminder run'; it cannot read the table, cannot send a message, and
cannot invoke anything else in the account.
